worksheet.title: What Comes Next?
worksheet.subtitle: Reading a pattern that repeats
worksheet.learning_goal: I can read a pattern and draw what comes next.

parts.title: Patterns repeat
parts.text: A pattern is a row that repeats the same way. If you know the pattern, you can tell what comes next.

parts.title: Watch Bit — ▲ ■ ▲ ■ …
parts.note: It goes triangle, square, triangle, square. After ▲ comes ■. The next one is ■.

parts.title: Draw what comes next
parts.prompt: Read the pattern out loud, then draw the next shape in the dashed box.

parts.title: Draw what comes next
parts.prompt: Read the pattern, then draw the next shape in the dashed box.

parts.title: You try — a longer pattern
parts.prompt: This pattern goes two-then-one. Read it and draw what comes next.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Reading a pattern lets you know what comes next. Computers follow patterns too — that is how they repeat a job the same way every time.

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children read a repeating shape pattern and draw the next shape. Reading and continuing a pattern is a first thinking-skill behind coding — it is how computers repeat a job the same way every time. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper and a pencil or crayon. You read each prompt aloud; the child draws the next shape. Optional: pattern blocks or beads to build the pattern by hand first.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Point and say the pattern aloud — "triangle, square, triangle, square…" The next is a square.
2. Do one together. Exercise 1 — say circle, star, circle, star, circle aloud; the next is a star.
3. Let them try. Children do Exercise 2, then Exercise 3 (the two-then-one pattern) on their own.

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — circle, star, circle, star, circle → next is a star. Exercise 2 — square, triangle, square, triangle → next is a square.
Exercise 3 — star, star, circle, star, star, circle → next is a star (the pattern is star, star, circle, repeating).

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: copying the last shape shown. Have them say the whole pattern aloud first.
Make it easier: build the pattern with real blocks and add the next one by hand.
Make it harder: ask the child to keep the pattern going for two or three more shapes.
Make it active: clap–stomp–clap–stomp and ask what movement comes next.

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children identify, reproduce, and extend repeating patterns.
In plain terms: spotting a repeating pattern and saying what comes next.
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child answers by drawing or circling.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child says the repeating part aloud and draws the correct next shape for each pattern.
